findings.evidence: Fiber.lean:120-125 uses `[CommGroup G]` and `(x : G)` as summand; mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Group/Finset/Defs.lean:750 `Equiv.prod_comp (e : ι ≃ κ) (g : κ → M) : ∏ i, g (e i) = ∏ i, g i` is the general form. PR description: the target sum is `Σ_{fP=Q} (P)` in the divisor group.
findings.fix: State `theorem MonoidHom.prod_fiber_eq_prod_ker {G H M : Type*} [Group G] [MulOneClass H] [CommMonoid M] (f : G →* H) {b : H} {a : G} (ha : f a = b) [Fintype {x : G // f x = b}] [Fintype f.ker] (g : G → M) : (∏ x : {x : G // f x = b}, g x) = ∏ t : f.ker, g (a * t)`, proved by `Equiv.prod_comp (f.subtypeFiberEquivKer ha).symm g` plus the coe simp lemma; drop `CommGroup G` to `Group G`.
findings.issue: `prod_fiber_eq_prod_ker` is stated only for the summand `(x : G)`, which forces `[CommGroup G]`. Mathlib's reindexing lemmas (`Equiv.prod_comp`, `Fintype.prod_equiv`) take an arbitrary `g : ι → M` into a `CommMonoid M`; the stated form is the `g = id` special case and does not apply to the PR's own motivating use, the divisor pullback `f*((Q)) = Σ_{fP=Q} (P)`, whose summand is the image of `P` in the divisor group, not `P`.

findings.evidence: Fiber.lean:121-125; contrast mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Group/Finset/Defs.lean:733-750, where both index types carry assumed `Fintype` instances rather than ones constructed in the statement.
findings.fix: Take `[Fintype {x : G // f x = b}]` as an ordinary instance argument (as in `Fintype.prod_equiv`) and delete both `letI`s; the equivalence still supplies the proof.
findings.issue: The statement binds its own `Fintype {x : G // f x = b}` via `letI := Fintype.ofEquiv f.ker (f.subtypeFiberEquivKer ha).symm`. A caller who already has a `Fintype` on the fiber (e.g. from `Fintype.ofFinite` after `finite_fiber`, or a decidability-derived one) gets a different instance term, so the LHS does not match and the lemma needs `convert`/`Subsingleton.elim` to use.

summary: The product lemma is stated at the wrong level: only for the identity summand (forcing CommGroup G) where Mathlib's analogous reindexing lemmas take an arbitrary function into a CommMonoid, and it pins a letI-built Fintype instance in the statement. The other three declarations sit at the natural level.
